text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright gave the Balts more words to cheer them up: while visiting Russia, she once again stressed the Balts would one day be admitted to NATO.

- German authorities are reported to have arrested Armands Stendzenieks, a Latvian who owes $18 million to the notorious Banka Baltija and which was allegedly guaranteed by Ventspils Nafta. He may soon be extradited to Latvia.
- It us still unclear whether Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans will step down after the prosecutor's office confirmed he had broken the anti-corruption law.

- Meeting in Riga, Latvian and Russian officials worked out a first draft of an agreement on co-operation in the social security sphere. The agreement is expected to solve the problems of people who worked in one country but then moved to another.
- The budget had a surplus of 14.6 million lats on July 9.
- A Finnish-Latvian joint venture, Detroit Group Latvia, signed a contract to lease the industrial premises of RAF, the financially-troubled Latvian minivan-maker. Production may resume next week.
